class SurfaceMesh : public std::enable_shared_from_this<SurfaceMesh>#
#include <surface_mesh.h>

A triangle mesh stored in OpenVCAD’s canonical vertex/index representation.

SurfaceMesh stores vertices, indexed triangles, and a bounding box. It can be constructed from explicit mesh data, files, VTK data, implicit trees, and SDF data. Derived data is built lazily and cached on the mesh: the geometry fingerprint, the selection topology, and an AABB tree used by ray, closest-point, and visibility queries. Signed-distance sampling accelerators remain in the compiler and sampler layers. CGAL closed-mesh validation is disabled by default; pass disable_validation=false to opt in.

std::shared_ptr<SurfaceMesh> clipped(const std::shared_ptr<Node> &node, const std::string &keep = "inside", const std::optional<double> &voxel_size = std::nullopt) const#

Clips the mesh by the zero level of a node’s signed distance field.

Triangles that cross the zero level are split at the crossing, which is located on the node itself, so plane, primitive, and expression cuts leave a clean open boundary. The node is prepared by this call.

Parameters:

  • node – Any OpenVCAD node; inside is where its signed distance is negative.

  • keep – “inside” keeps the part where the node is negative, “outside” the rest.

  • voxel_size – Voxel size in millimetres used to prepare the node. Empty uses the mean mesh edge length.

Returns:

The clipped open mesh.

std::shared_ptr<SurfaceMesh> decimated(const std::optional<size_t> &target_count = std::nullopt, const std::optional<double> &target_ratio = std::nullopt, const std::optional<double> &max_error = std::nullopt) const#

Simplifies the mesh by edge collapse with Garland-Heckbert quadric error.

Give a target face count or ratio, an error bound, or a target plus a bound. Borders and label boundaries are preserved as well as the quadrics allow; label boundaries are never collapsed.

Parameters:

  • target_count – Stop once the mesh has at most this many triangles.

  • target_ratio – Stop once the mesh has at most this fraction of its triangles (0, 1].

  • max_error – Stop once the cheapest collapse would move the surface farther than about this distance in millimetres from the original face planes.

Returns:

The simplified mesh.

std::shared_ptr<SurfaceMesh> remove_small_components(const std::optional<double> &min_volume = std::nullopt, const std::optional<size_t> &min_triangles = std::nullopt, bool keep_largest = false) const#

Removes small disconnected pieces such as floating islands.

Pieces are grouped into bodies first: an inward-facing cavity surface belongs to the smallest outward surface that encloses it, so a hollow part keeps its inner wall and is judged by its material volume.

Parameters:

  • min_volume – Remove bodies whose enclosed volume is below this value (mm^3).

  • min_triangles – Remove bodies with fewer triangles than this.

  • keep_largest – If true, keep only the body with the largest volume.

Returns:

The cleaned mesh.

std::shared_ptr<MeshSelection> select_visible_from(const std::vector<glm::vec3> &seed_points, const std::string &facing = "any", const std::optional<double> &max_view_angle_degrees = std::nullopt)#

Selects triangles that can be seen from any of the seed points.

A triangle is visible when a straight line from a seed reaches one of its interior sample points before hitting any other triangle. The result crosses sharp creases freely, which makes it suited to picking the inner surface of a shell as seen from points inside it.

Parameters:

  • seed_points – Viewpoints in millimetres.

  • facing – “any”, “toward” (the triangle normal points at the seed), or “away”.

  • max_view_angle_degrees – Optional largest angle between the triangle normal (or its reverse for “any”) and the direction to the seed.

Returns:

The selection of visible triangles.

Public Static Functions

static double sdf_lipschitz_bound(const SDF_Grid &grid, const glm::vec3 &box_min, const glm::vec3 &box_max, double bandwidth, double offset = 0.0)#

Measures a Lipschitz bound of a band-clipped, box-capped signed-distance grid.

The field is the one the grid-backed leaves (Mesh, TexturedMesh, CAD in fast mode) return: F(p) = trilinear(p) - offset, the grid read with OpenVDB’s BoxSampler, capped as max(F(p), signed_distance_to_box(p)) inside the box padded by the bandwidth T, and no value (counted as T) beyond it. Inside one grid cell, each partial derivative of the trilinear interpolant is a convex combination of that axis’s four edge differences over the spacing, so |grad F| <= sqrt(rx^2 + ry^2 + rz^2) with r the largest edge difference per axis (at most sqrt(3) times the largest difference between neighbouring values). The bound is the largest of these over every cell a point of the padded box can read, with one cell of slack, using the values the sampler reads: active and inactive voxels, tiles and the background. Cells whose eight values are all at least T (G is T there) or all at most -T (G is the clipped box distance there) are skipped. The box distance and the clamp to [-T, T] are 1-Lipschitz, and at the face of the padded box the box distance is at least T, so the clipped value is continuous into “no value”. Regions of 8^3 voxels with no leaf node hold one tile or background value each, so they are checked as one cell. The result covers the trilinear field exactly; the sampler’s float arithmetic adds a few float ulps of the values and coordinates on top.

Parameters:

  • grid – A grid with an axis-aligned scale transform, as compute_sdf() builds.

  • box_min – The minimum of the node’s bounding box.

  • box_max – The maximum of the node’s bounding box.

  • bandwidth – The bandwidth T the node was prepared with.

  • offset – The amount subtracted from every grid value (a Mesh’s sdf_shim).

Returns:

The bound (at least 1), or infinity if the grid’s transform is not an axis-aligned scale or a value is not finite.

static double signed_distance_to_box(double x, double y, double z, const glm::vec3 &box_min, const glm::vec3 &box_max)#

Returns the signed Euclidean distance from a point to an axis-aligned box.

Positive outside (the distance to the nearest box point), negative inside (minus the distance to the nearest face). It is 1-Lipschitz and at least the per-axis distance to the box outside it.

Parameters:

  • x – The x coordinate.

  • y – The y coordinate.

  • z – The z coordinate.

  • box_min – The box minimum.

  • box_max – The box maximum.

Returns:

The signed distance.

struct VolumeMeshingOptions#
#include <surface_mesh.h>

Controls how a signed-distance volume is turned into triangles.

The defaults reproduce OpenVCAD’s uniform meshing, where every voxel the surface passes through contributes polygons.

Public Members

double adaptivity = 0.0#

OpenVDB surface adaptivity from 0 (uniform) to 1 (most simplified).

Voxels inside one 8^3 block merge into one polygon vertex when their surface normals differ by less than an angle with 1 - cos(angle) = adaptivity (0.01 is about 8 degrees, 0.05 about 18, 0.1 about 26). Flat regions merge at any value, sharp detail keeps voxel resolution, and the surface stays closed.

bool relax_disoriented_triangles = true#

Relaxes triangles whose orientation disagrees with the field gradient.

Only used when adaptivity is greater than zero.

struct MeshHit#

class MeshSelection#
#include <mesh_selection.h>

An immutable set of triangle IDs tied to one SurfaceMesh state.

MeshSelection keeps the source mesh alive and records its geometry fingerprint when the selection is created. Operations fail if the source is later mutated, preventing stale triangle IDs from being applied to different geometry. Selection operations are intentionally permissive about patch topology; conversion to TriangleMeshSurface is the boundary that validates the connected, manifold, genus-0 open patch (holes allowed) that flattening requires.

Measures the distance along each ray to its first intersection with a triangle mesh.

One distance per ray, or NaN where nothing is hit within max_distance.

std::vector<double> ray_distances_to_node(const std::vector<glm::vec3> &origins, const std::vector<glm::vec3> &directions, const std::shared_ptr<Node> &target, double max_distance, double tolerance = 1e-3, double voxel_size = 0.25)#

Measures the distance along each ray to the first zero crossing of a node’s field.

The target is cloned and the clone is prepared with voxel_size and a bandwidth of max_distance, so the caller’s node is untouched. Each ray is marched with sphere tracing: steps are the absolute field value (never smaller than tolerance), a hit is a value within tolerance of zero or a sign change, and a sign change is refined by bisection to tolerance. Sign-change detection keeps the march robust for approximate distance fields. Rays are traced in parallel with one target clone per thread.

Typical use: the gap from every vertex of a head patch along its normal to a helmet shell, to drive a variable-height CellMap.

Parameters:

  • origins – Ray start points in mm.

  • directions – Ray directions; normalized internally and required to be non-zero.

  • target – The node whose zero level set is hit.

  • max_distance – Positive maximum ray length in mm.

  • tolerance – Positive hit tolerance in mm.

  • voxel_size – Positive voxel size in mm used to prepare the target clone.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – if the counts differ, a ray is not finite or has a zero direction, target is null, or max_distance, tolerance or voxel_size is not positive and finite.

Returns:

One distance per ray, or NaN where nothing is hit within max_distance.

class TriangleMeshSurface : public ParametricSurface#
#include <triangle_mesh_surface.h>

An immutable triangle-mesh disk patch exposed as a near-conformally parameterized surface with a trimmed, natural-shape chart.

TriangleMeshSurface takes an open triangle mesh that is topologically a disk and flattens it into a 2D chart so a discrete mesh can drive the same structured CellMap machinery as an exact CAD face.

Parameterization: the flattening method is selectable. The default “lscm” flattens with free-boundary least-squares conformal maps (LSCM, Levy et al. 2002) pinning only two vertices, so the chart takes the patch’s natural outline instead of being forced onto a square. “arap” flattens with the as-rigid-as-possible energy (Liu et al. 2008), which balances angle and area distortion on a free boundary. “authalic” flattens with the iterative area-preserving parameterizer (Jain et al. 2019) on a circular arc-length border, trading angle fidelity for near-uniform area. Whichever method is chosen, the chart is then fitted into its axis-aligned bounding rectangle, which uv_bounds() reports with the longer side normalized to exactly 1. The chart does not fill that rectangle: the region between the chart boundary and the rectangle is outside the surface, and contains() reports it as such so CellMap trimming can deactivate it.

Injective fallback: none of the primary methods guarantees a one-to-one chart. When the requested chart folds (flipped or collapsed chart triangles, or a failed global overlap check), the surface automatically falls back to Floater mean-value coordinates on a circular arc-length border (Floater 2003, Tutte 1963), whose positive convex-combination weights on a convex border guarantee an injective chart at the cost of more shape distortion. parameterization_method() reports which parameterizer produced the chart. Only when both fail is the patch rejected.

Orientation control: the chart’s u-axis becomes the lattice’s first logical direction, so it is chosen deliberately instead of inheriting the solver’s arbitrary rotation. By default the chart is rotated so its principal axis (area-weighted covariance of the flattened triangles) runs along +u with a deterministic sign, which gives elongated patches an elongated, axis-aligned chart rectangle; near-isotropic charts keep the solver’s orientation. Alternatively an optional world-space hint direction is projected onto the patch and the chart is rotated so that direction runs along +u.

Input requirements: the mesh must be a single connected, edge-manifold and vertex-manifold component with consistent winding, at least one boundary loop, and genus 0 (Euler characteristic V - E + F = 2 - boundary loops). Closed meshes, handles, disconnected components, and non-manifold configurations are each rejected with a distinct message.

Holes are trims: a patch may carry interior openings (vents, cut-outs), which makes it a genus-0 patch with several boundary loops. The longest boundary loop (by world-space length) is the outer edge; every other loop is a hole. Each hole is filled internally, for the parameterization only, with a refined and faired patch (CGAL hole filling, which keeps tangent continuity with the surrounding surface), so the whole patch flattens like a disk and the chart stays smooth across the opening. This mirrors how a trimmed CAD face maps its untrimmed parent surface. The filled triangles are trimmed: point() and normal() evaluate on the fill so CellMap cells spanning a hole stay well-conditioned, but contains() reports every chart coordinate inside a hole as off the surface. CellMap trimming therefore removes the lattice from the openings and seals their walls exactly as it handles the outer edge. If faired filling fails for a hole, a refined unfaired fill is used, then a centroid fan as a last resort. The accessors vertices(), triangles(), uv_coordinates(), vertex_normals(), and mesh() always describe the input patch; fill vertices are appended internally after the input vertices.

Orientation: input triangle winding defines the positive normal direction, and therefore the positive height direction of any CellMap built from this surface. Normals are angle-weighted vertex normals interpolated barycentrically, so the offset direction stays continuous across triangle edges. Smooth normals deliberately round sharp creases, and large offsets can still self-intersect; CellMap’s own Jacobian diagnostics remain the authoritative check on the final volume.

virtual bool contains(double u, double v, double tolerance = 1e-7) const override#

Tests whether chart coordinates lie on the parameterized patch.

This is a real point-in-chart test against the flattened triangles, so the empty region between the chart outline and the bounding rectangle reports false. Chart coordinates inside a filled hole also report false, because only the input triangles count as the surface. CellMap trimming uses exactly this predicate to deactivate cells beyond the patch’s true boundary and inside its holes.

class ParametricSurface#
#include <parametric_surface.h>

Abstract contract for a surface that can be evaluated on a rectangular UV domain.

Implementations expose a bounded parameter rectangle, an oriented point map, and an oriented unit normal. This is the minimum surface interface required to build a structured curvilinear CellMap, and it is shared by exact CAD faces and by parameterized triangle-mesh patches.

Coordinates: uv_bounds() reports the native parameter rectangle. Callers sample the rectangle by linear interpolation between its corners, so implementations must accept any coordinate inside those bounds. Implementations backed by a trimmed or non-rectangular domain report the enclosing rectangle and use contains() to report which coordinates actually lie on the surface.

Tolerance: contains() accepts a parametric tolerance so callers can treat boundary coordinates as inside. Implementations must remain stable and deterministic for coordinates exactly on a boundary.

Orientation: normal() returns the oriented unit normal that defines the positive offset direction of the surface. CellMap extrudes along this direction, so the sign convention of an implementation determines the sign convention of a signed-height map.

Subclassed by CADFace, TriangleMeshSurface

class ImageHeightField : public HeightField#
#include <height_field.h>

Immutable mip-filtered PNG height map.

PNG values are converted from the requested channel to [0, 1], then multiplied by amplitude_mm. (0, 0) is the lower-left image corner. The PNG is decoded at 16 bits per channel, and a box-filtered mip chain is built down to 1x1. sample() picks the level whose texel size matches the largest voxel edge and blends bilinear lookups of two levels. Clones share the immutable image data.

Tessellates every face into one welded, consistently oriented SurfaceMesh.

Triangles of reversed faces are flipped so solids face outward, nodes shared by neighbouring faces are welded within a small tolerance, and each triangle’s label is the index of its face in TopExp_Explorer order (CADModel::faces() order).

class CellMap#
#include <cell_map.h>

Immutable structured curvilinear map from logical unit cells to world space.

Logical coordinates cover [0, nu] x [0, nv] x [0, nw]. Linear maps use one trilinear element per cell; curved maps use eight sub-elements per cell so midpoint CAD samples are retained without runtime OCCT queries.

Public Types

enum class TrimMode#

Strategy for restricting a surface-built map to the surface’s true domain.

Surfaces backed by a trimmed or non-rectangular chart do not fill their UV bounding rectangle. TrimMode selects how the map treats the empty margin: keep it, remove whole logical elements, or clip implicitly at the true boundary curve.

Values:

enumerator none#

Keep the full rectangular logical domain; nothing is removed.

enumerator cells#

Deactivate whole structured elements outside the surface domain.

enumerator boundary#

Clip smoothly at the surface’s true boundary curve (default).

Public Functions

inline const std::vector<bool> &active_elements() const#

Returns the per-element activity mask, in element order.

Returns:

The activity mask.

CellMap(const glm::ivec3 &cells, int subdivisions, const std::vector<glm::vec3> &control_points, const std::array<bool, 3> &periodic = {false, false, false}, const std::vector<bool> &active_elements = {})#

Builds a map from explicit control points.

The map has cells * subdivisions structured elements per axis, each a trilinear hexahedron. Control points are ordered with U fastest, then V, then W. The world bounding box, the element BVH, and the boundary mesh are built here.

Parameters:

  • cells – Positive logical cell counts along U, V, and W.

  • subdivisions – Positive number of structured elements per cell along each axis.

  • control_points – (cells * subdivisions + 1) control points per axis, all finite.

  • periodic – Whether U, V, and W wrap through a seam.

  • active_elements – Per-element activity mask in element order, or empty for all active.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If a count is not positive, the control-point or mask size does not match, or a control point is not finite.

Returns the logical cell counts along U, V, and W.

Returns:

The cell counts.

Boundary-trim clipping inside an active element is not applied here.

Returns:

True if the point is in an active element.

The control points.

Return signed distance to the finite active CellMap domain.

The boundary is represented by an accelerated triangle mesh extracted from exposed structured-element faces. Distance is negative inside the active map, zero on its boundary, and positive outside. Periodic seams are not boundaries.

world – World-coordinate query point.

world – World-coordinate query point.

Unsigned distance to the active map boundary.

double edge_unsigned_distance(const glm::vec3 &world) const#

Return the unsigned distance to the map’s edge wall.

The edge wall is the side boundary of the active domain: the exposed element faces along the logical U and V perimeter and, for boundary-trimmed maps, the smooth trim wall swept from the surface’s cropped edge through the map height. The base and offset surfaces of the map are deliberately excluded, so this measures distance to the cropped lattice edges only.

Parameters:

world – World-coordinate query point.

Returns:

Unsigned distance to the edge wall.

std::optional<CellMapLocation> locate(const glm::vec3 &world, double tolerance = 1e-6, size_t max_iterations = 24) const#

Locate a world-space point and retain its deterministic cell ownership.

The answer for the most recent query (point, tolerance, iterations) is cached per thread and per map, so several mapped nodes sharing one map (a lattice unioned with its rim, a domain, attribute adapters) invert each sample point once. Cached answers are the exact same values, so results are bit-identical with or without the cache. Boundary-trimmed regions are rejected.

Parameters:

  • world – World-space point to locate.

  • tolerance – Requested Newton convergence tolerance, clamped as in inverse().

  • max_iterations – Maximum damped Newton iterations per candidate element.

Throws:

static std::shared_ptr<CellMap> from_surface(const std::shared_ptr<ParametricSurface> &surface, const glm::ivec3 &cells, const std::shared_ptr<FloatAttribute> &height, bool linear = false, TrimMode trim = TrimMode::boundary, double standoff = 0.0)#

Builds a variable-height map by extruding a parametric surface along its normal.

Identical to the constant-height factory except that the height is a scalar field. It is sampled once per control column, at the column’s base point on the surface (world coordinates, signed-distance argument 0), so the map spans [standoff, standoff + height(p)] along the oriented normal at every column. A constant field reproduces the constant-height map exactly. The field must be finite, non-zero, and of one sign at every column; the sign selects the side of the surface exactly as a constant height does. Use TriangleMeshSurface::vertex_field() for per-vertex heights, for example the ray-cast gap from a head patch to a shell (see ray_distances_to_mesh()), so the cells end on the target. Strongly varying heights can still fold the volume, which the Jacobian validation reports.

Parameters:

  • surface – The surface to extrude.

  • cells – Logical cell counts along U, V, and the height direction.

  • height – Signed height field in mm sampled at surface base points.

  • linear – True for one trilinear element per cell, false to retain midpoint samples.

  • trim – How to restrict the map to the surface’s valid domain.

  • standoff – Signed stand-off distance along the surface normal at which the map begins, sharing the sign convention of height.

Returns:

The validated structured map.

Builds a signed-height map by extruding a parametric surface along its normal.

This is the generic implementation shared by exact CAD faces and parameterized triangle-mesh patches. The sign of height follows the surface’s oriented normal, so input orientation determines which side of the surface is filled. A non-zero standoff lifts the whole map off the surface, so it spans [standoff, standoff + height] along the oriented normal.

static std::shared_ptr<CellMap> warp(const std::shared_ptr<CellMap> &base, const std::shared_ptr<FloatAttribute> &u_scale, const std::shared_ptr<FloatAttribute> &v_scale, const std::shared_ptr<FloatAttribute> &w_scale, bool lock_u_bounds = true, bool lock_v_bounds = true, bool lock_w_bounds = true)#

Builds a new map with the same cells as base but a graded cell spacing.

Along each axis, every element’s logical width is weighted by exp(clamp(s, -4, 4)), where s is the scale attribute sampled at the element’s midpoint on the base map (world position from the unwarped base map, with the map’s logical and cell context set). The scale is therefore a natural-log exponent: 0 or a null attribute keeps the spacing uniform. With a locked axis the weights are normalized so both boundaries stay fixed; with an unlocked axis each element’s width is multiplied by its weight, so the far boundary moves (the base map is continued linearly past its end) and logical 0 stays. The requested coordinates are smoothed, and if the result fails validate() the warp is blended back toward the base map, halving its strength each time, until it is valid. The result keeps the base map’s cells, subdivisions, periodicity, active elements, and trim mode.

Parameters:

  • base – The map to warp. It must not carry a boundary trim (see has_boundary_trim()).

  • u_scale – Log-scale exponent field for U element widths, or nullptr for 0.

  • v_scale – Log-scale exponent field for V element widths, or nullptr for 0.

  • w_scale – Log-scale exponent field for W element widths, or nullptr for 0.

  • lock_u_bounds – Keep both U boundaries fixed and only redistribute elements.

  • lock_v_bounds – Keep both V boundaries fixed and only redistribute elements.

  • lock_w_bounds – Keep both W boundaries fixed and only redistribute elements.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If base is null or has a boundary trim (TrimMode::boundary, the default for the surface factories), if a scale attribute returns a non-finite or non-scalar value, or if the warp still folds the map at 1e-4 of its strength.

Returns:

The warped map.

class FieldWarpMap : public WarpMap#
#include <warp_map.h>

A warp given by a vector field: g(p) is the field’s value at p.

The field is any Vec3Attribute (three expressions, numba callbacks, a vector volume, …), sampled with d = 0. It has no closed-form Jacobian or bounds, so a Warp built from it takes central differences and needs explicit bounds. Vec3Attribute returns single precision, so the finite-difference step should stay well above 1e-6 of the coordinate size; Warp picks it from the voxel size.

class WarpMap : public CoordinateSource#
#include <warp_map.h>

A deformation of space, described by where each world point pulls back to in its child.

A Warp node samples its child at g(p), the child point that world point p pulls back to. WarpMap is that g. Subclasses implement to_child(); the Warp node does the rest (distance correction, attributes, bounding box, cloning). See deforming_space_architecture.md.

The Jacobian J = dg/dp drives the distance correction. The default jacobian() takes central differences of to_child(); maps with a closed form override it, which is faster and free of finite-difference noise.

Coordinates: every map is a CoordinateSource with “child_x”, “child_y” and “child_z” (where a point pulls back to), followed by the map’s own natural coordinates, named in the constructor, so material and other geometry can be graded along them.

Thread safety: to_child() may sample fields that keep per-call state, so each evaluation thread uses its own clone(). Immutable data (tables, frames) is shared between clones.

Subclassed by BendMap, DisplacementMap, FieldWarpMap, SphereWrapMap, TaperMap, TwistMap

class AxisLaw#
#include <deformation_maps.h>

The running integral of a rate along an axis: L(h) = integral from 0 to h of rate.

Twist and taper are rates per unit length along an axis. A constant rate gives L(h) = rate * h. A field rate is read along the axis, at origin + h * axis with d = 0, and integrated once (trapezoids on a fine table) over the range it is built for; beyond the table the end rates continue. The law is immutable after construction, so clones of a map share it.

class BendMap : public WarpMap#
#include <deformation_maps.h>

Bends space around an axis: straight lines along a direction become circles of a given radius.

The bend happens in a frame (centre line point c, unit vectors e_x, e_y, e_z): a world point is c + rho (sin(theta) e_x - cos(theta) e_z) + y e_y, with rho its distance from the centre line (through c along e_y) and theta its angle. It pulls back to the child point child_origin + (R theta) cx + y cy + (R - rho) cz: arc length at radius R becomes length along cx, and distance inside radius R becomes distance along cz. Lengths on the circle of radius R (the neutral surface) are kept. theta runs over [angle_start, angle_start + 2 pi).

Warp::bend() places the child frame on the bend frame, so the child stays put where theta = 0. Warp::wrap_cylinder() uses a fixed flat-design frame instead.

Coordinates: “angle” (theta, in degrees) and “radius” (rho).

World bounds: exact for the annular sector holding the child’s box.

class SphereWrapMap : public WarpMap#
#include <deformation_maps.h>

Wraps a flat design onto a sphere: child x and y are arc lengths of longitude and latitude.

A world point at distance r from the centre, longitude lon (counter-clockwise about the north axis from the reference direction, in [0, 2 pi)) and latitude lat (from the equator, in [-pi/2, pi/2]) pulls back to the child point (R lon, R lat, r - R). The design’s z = 0 plane lies on the sphere of radius R and z grows outward. This is the equirectangular wrap: lengths along the equator and along meridians are kept, while parallels shrink by cos(lat), so a design is squeezed narrower toward the poles. Keep it away from them (|y| < R pi / 2), where the longitude is undefined. The Jacobian is analytic.

Coordinates: “longitude” and “latitude” (degrees) and “radius” (r).

World bounds: the sphere holding the child’s outermost layer.

class TaperMap : public WarpMap#
#include <deformation_maps.h>

Scales the section perpendicular to an axis by a factor that changes along the axis.

The scale at height h = (p - origin) . axis is s(h) = 1 + integral from 0 to h of rate, so a constant rate is a linear taper and s is 1 at the origin. g(p) keeps the height and divides the offset from the axis by s(h). s must stay positive over the child’s axial extent. The Jacobian is analytic.

Coordinates: “scale” (s) and “height” (h).

World bounds: the child’s box corners scaled about the axis by the smallest and largest s.

class TwistMap : public WarpMap#
#include <deformation_maps.h>

Twists space about an axis: the section at height h turns by the integral of the rate.

The angle at height h = (p - origin) . axis is theta(h) = integral from 0 to h of rate, in degrees, counter-clockwise about the axis; it is zero at the origin. g(p) turns p back by -theta(h) about the axis. The Jacobian is analytic: R(-theta) - theta’(h) (a x q) a^T, where q is the turned-back offset from the axis point.

Coordinates: “angle” (theta, in degrees) and “height” (h).

World bounds: the cylinder about the axis holding the child’s box over its axial extent.

class DisplacementMap : public WarpMap#
#include <displacement_map.h>

Moves material by a displacement field: material at X moves to X + u(X).

Frame: u is sampled at the undeformed point X, in the child’s coordinates, and is a vector in those same coordinates (which are the Warp’s own: world, when the Warp is the root). This is the convention of simulation results, whose displacements live on the undeformed part. u is sampled with d = 0.

Pull-back: g(p) is the X with X + u(X) = p. It is found by fixed-point iteration X <- p - u(X), starting from p - u(p), which converges while u changes by less than the distance it is sampled over (|grad u| < 1). If the iteration stalls, Newton steps with a finite-difference grad u take over, which converge wherever the deformation is invertible. Points that still do not converge use the best estimate and are counted (failed_inversions(), shared by all clones).

prepare() checks det(I + grad u) on a grid in and near the material and throws if the displacement folds material onto itself, since no pull-back exists there.

Jacobian: dg/dp = (I + grad u(X))^-1, with grad u by central differences at X.

World bounds: the child’s box widened by the largest displacement sampled over it on each axis, plus a quarter of it as margin.

Coordinates: “displacement” (|u(X)|, how far the material at a point moved).

class HexahedralMesh#
#include <hexahedral_mesh.h>

Pure geometric structured hexahedral mesh generated from an implicit OpenVCAD tree.

The mesh stores explicit node positions and hexahedral connectivity. It contains no solver-specific or attribute-export logic. The root’s bounding box is split into a grid of voxel_size cells; a cell becomes an element when the tree’s signed distance at its centre is <= 0. Unused grid nodes are dropped.

Parameters:

  • directory – The directory containing the DICOM stack.

  • rescale_slope – Slope applied to raw pixel values to get Hounsfield units. The default (negative infinity) reads it from the metadata.

  • rescale_intercept – Intercept added after the slope. The default reads it from the metadata.

  • slice_thickness – Voxel size along z, in mm. The default reads it from the metadata.

  • x_pixel_spacing – Voxel size along x, in mm. The default reads it from the metadata.

  • y_pixel_spacing – Voxel size along y, in mm. The default reads it from the metadata.

  • slice_order – How the slice files are ordered into a stack. See DICOMSliceOrder.

  • filename_prefix – A literal filename prefix ignored when the order falls back to filenames. Use it when the fixed part of a filename contains digits that must not take part in the ordering (for example “scan2024_” in “scan2024_001.dcm”).

  • origin – The world-space position, in mm, of the volume’s minimum corner. Defaults to the coordinate system origin.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – if a value left at its default is missing from the metadata.

Functions

SeedBlendResult blend_seed_sets(const std::shared_ptr<Node> &host, const std::vector<glm::vec3> &random_points, const std::vector<glm::vec3> &regular_points, const std::shared_ptr<FloatAttribute> &regularity, double match_radius, double minimum_separation, double boundary_clearance = 0.0)#

Morph a random seed set into a regular site set with a regularity field.

Regularity w is sampled at every site and random point and clamped to [0, 1]. Regular sites with w > 0 are paired with random points with w < 1 by greedy nearest matching within match_radius (shortest pairs first). A pair becomes one seed at q + w(r) (r - q), so seeds slide from their random positions (w = 0) onto the regular sites (w = 1) while the seed count stays the same. Unpaired regular sites are kept where w >= 0.5, unpaired random points where w < 0.5. Finally seeds closer than minimum_separation to a seed with higher regularity are dropped, which removes slivers that would create tiny Voronoi cells. When a host is given, a blended seed that falls outside it is moved to whichever source point is inside.

Parameters:

  • host – Optional prepared host (may be null).

  • random_points – Random seeds, for example from sample_poisson_seeds().

  • regular_points – Regular lattice sites.

  • regularity – Regularity field; 0 keeps random seeds, 1 keeps regular sites.

  • match_radius – Maximum pairing distance in millimetres.

  • minimum_separation – Minimum distance between output seeds (0 disables the check).

  • boundary_clearance – Host clearance used for the containment check.

Returns:

Blended seeds and their provenance.

SeedBlendResult jitter_seed_sites(const std::shared_ptr<Node> &host, const std::vector<glm::vec3> &regular_points, const std::shared_ptr<FloatAttribute> &regularity, double amplitude, uint64_t seed, double minimum_separation, double boundary_clearance = 0.0)#

Randomly displace regular sites by an amount that falls to zero where w = 1.

Each site r moves to r + (1 - w(r)) * amplitude * u, with u uniform in the unit ball and drawn from a per-site stream, so results do not depend on order. This is the classic “perturbed lattice” route from a regular Voronoi foam (w = 1) to an irregular one. Displacements that would leave the host or come closer than minimum_separation to an already placed seed are redrawn (up to 16 times) and then shrunk towards the site.

Parameters:

  • host – Optional prepared host (may be null).

  • regular_points – Regular lattice sites.

  • regularity – Regularity field sampled at the sites and clamped to [0, 1].

  • amplitude – Maximum displacement in millimetres where w = 0.

  • seed – Random seed.

  • minimum_separation – Minimum distance between output seeds (0 disables the check).

  • boundary_clearance – Host clearance used for the containment check.

Returns:

Displaced seeds with regular_index set to the source site.

PoissonSeedResult sample_poisson_seeds(const std::shared_ptr<Node> &host, const std::shared_ptr<FloatAttribute> &spacing, uint64_t seed, size_t max_count = 0, double boundary_clearance = 0.0, size_t attempts_per_point = 30)#

Sample variable-spacing Poisson-disk seeds inside a prepared host.

Uses Bridson’s active-list growth with a uniform background grid, followed by rounds of random darts that restart growth in host regions the front never reached (disconnected or narrow parts). Two points are accepted together when their distance is at least the mean of their local spacings, the same rule as the Python sample_points_in_host(). The spacing field is sampled at candidate positions with the host signed distance as its d argument. Results depend only on the inputs and seed.

Parameters:

  • host – Prepared implicit host; a point is inside when its SDF is <= -boundary_clearance.

  • spacing – Positive, finite local spacing field in millimetres.

  • seed – Random seed.

  • max_count – Maximum number of points, or 0 for no limit other than saturation.

  • boundary_clearance – Non-negative distance kept between seeds and the host surface.

  • attempts_per_point – Candidates tried around each active point (Bridson’s k).

Returns:

Accepted points and statistics.

SurfaceSeedResult sample_surface_poisson_seeds(const SurfaceMesh &mesh, const std::shared_ptr<FloatAttribute> &spacing, uint64_t seed, size_t max_count = 0, size_t attempts_per_point = 30)#

Sample variable-spacing Poisson-disk seeds on a triangle surface.

Darts land uniformly by area: a triangle is chosen in proportion to its area and a point uniformly inside it. A dart is kept when its Euclidean distance to every kept point is at least the mean of their local spacings, the same rule as sample_poisson_seeds(). Sampling stops after a long run of rejected darts (attempts_per_point times the number of points, and at least 64 times that), which leaves the surface close to saturated. Each dart needs only its own triangle, so open, non-manifold or noisy scanned meshes work. The spacing field is sampled at each dart with d = 0. Distances are straight-line, so keep the spacing below the thickness of thin walls and the gap between nearby sheets. Results depend only on the inputs.

Parameters:

  • mesh – Triangle surface; degenerate triangles are ignored.

  • spacing – Positive, finite local spacing field in millimetres.

  • seed – Random seed.

  • max_count – Maximum number of points, or 0 for no limit other than saturation.

  • attempts_per_point – Rejected darts allowed per kept point before sampling stops.

Returns:

Accepted points, their triangles and spacings, and statistics.

std::vector<size_t> select_points_in_host(const std::shared_ptr<Node> &host, const std::vector<glm::vec3> &points, double boundary_clearance = 0.0)#

SurfaceVoronoi restricted_voronoi(const SurfaceMesh &mesh, const std::vector<glm::vec3> &seeds)#

Compute the restricted Voronoi diagram of seed points on a triangle surface.

This is the 3D Voronoi diagram of the seeds intersected with the surface: the region of a seed is the part of the surface closer to it than to any other seed. Every triangle is handled on its own, so open, non-manifold or noisy scanned meshes work. A Voronoi cell is convex, so a triangle whose three corners have the same nearest seed belongs to that seed whole. Any other triangle is clipped exactly against the bisector planes of every seed that can own part of it (all seeds within min_v d(v) + 3 r of its centroid, where d(v) is a corner’s nearest-seed distance and r the largest centroid-to-corner distance). Triangles run in parallel; the result does not depend on the thread count. Seeds need not lie on the surface, but seeds sampled on it (sample_surface_poisson_seeds()) give the expected cells.

Parameters:

  • mesh – Triangle surface; degenerate triangles are ignored.

  • seeds – Finite seed points.

Returns:

The boundary pieces and the area each seed owns.

class PointGrid#
#include <point_grid.h>

A uniform bucket grid over indexed points for radius and nearest-point queries.

Points are stored by index; the caller keeps their coordinates. Points outside the grid’s box are clamped into the border cells, so queries stay exact for any point. The cell size grows when the grid would exceed about 32 million cells. Used by the seed samplers and the restricted Voronoi diagram.
